data.narrative:
BRINC Drones is a Series C-stage defense and security drone company founded by Blake Resnick that has raised $157M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 12 same-sector peers at equivalent or adjacent funding stages, comprising 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private companies including Quantum-Systems, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $157M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yields $267M. Peer-median analysis across the 12-company comparable set produces $1.8B, with a range of $300M to $18.0B reflecting significant dispersion driven by outliers like Helsing ($18.0B) and Quantum-Systems ($8.0B). The latter peers represent later-stage or higher-velocity companies within the defense tech sector.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $227M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.0B. This wide spread reflects material uncertainty around BRINC's growth trajectory relative to peer performance and the early-stage nature of the defense-tech market. Key uncertainties include customer concentration, regulatory pathway clarity, and competitive positioning versus better-funded peers. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively; peer multiples suggest substantially higher value, though peer heterogeneity limits precision.
